questions.q: Why are elections necessary in a democracy, and what makes an election democratic?
answer: In a large country it is impossible for everyone to govern together, so elections are the means by which people choose their representatives at regular intervals.

answer.text: Elections allow citizens to select those who will make decisions on their behalf, to judge the work of the government, and to change their rulers peacefully if dissatisfied, keeping the government accountable.

For an election to be democratic, everyone should be able to choose, through universal adult franchise; there should be a real choice of candidates and parties; elections should be held regularly; the ruling party should have a fair chance of losing; and the whole process must be conducted in a free and fair manner.

answer: Only when these conditions are met do elections truly serve democracy.

questions.q: Describe India's electoral system and the role of the Election Commission.

answer.text: India is divided into constituencies, and the voters of each elect one representative under the First-Past-The-Post system, in which the candidate with the most votes wins. Some constituencies are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to ensure their representation. Every citizen aged eighteen and above can vote, and voting is by secret ballot using Electronic Voting Machines with VVPAT.

Elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India, an independent constitutional body headed by the Chief Election Commissioner. It prepares the voter lists, fixes the schedule, enforces the Model Code of Conduct, and oversees the whole process, so that elections are largely free and fair.

questions.q: Why is universal adult franchise important, and how does it make Indian elections democratic?

answer.text: gives every citizen above a certain age the right to vote, and it is the foundation of democratic elections.

list: Every adult has one vote and every vote has equal value, regardless of wealth, education, caste, religion or sex
This makes political power rest with the people as a whole
Because everyone can vote, leaders must seek the support of ordinary people and address their needs
